newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks open mixed on Wall St weakness, interest rate fears.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks open mixed on Wall St weakness, interest rate fears.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were mixed in early trade on Thursday, partly undermined by falls on Wall Street and nervousness over interest rates, brokers said.
"Overall, I think we're going to see a fairly wishy-washy day," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
The Hang Seng Index was down 9.62 points or 0.08 percent at 12,697.42 after 25 minutes of trade. Turnover was HK$976.71 million.
Brokers expected consolidation among developers and banks, and some buying interest in H-shares after recent selling.
"There's nothing happening," said a head trader at a U.S. investment bank.
Brokers said they expected listlessness in Hong Kong stocks after Wednesday's gains and the softness overnight in New York.
On Wednesday, the Hang Seng Index rose sharply by 126.19 points to 12,707.04 while the Dow industrials fell 20.87 points to 6,812.72.
Brokers expected Swire Pacific Ltd shares to gain on news that a Swire unit had teamed up with Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd to develop the Shui Wing steel mill site in Hong Kong.
Swire has been buying back its shares in recent weeks.
"It seems quite quiet -- red chips are more active than the blue chips," said Michael Ng, dealing director with Sassoon Securities.
Brokers said the market was focusing on KEL Holdings Ltd and China Merchants Hai Hong Holdings Co Ltd, which said on Wednesday it would raise HK$3.86 billion through a new share issue.
KEL shares made their trading debut at HK$1.48, up from an issue price of HK$1.00, then eased to HK$1.32. China Merchants Hai Hong was up HK$0.55 at HK$7.10.
Swire led the gainers, rocketing HK$1.25 to HK$58.00.
Sun Hung Kai was up HK$0.25 at HK$81.25.
Exporter Li & Fung Ltd, which on Wednesday announced a 33 percent rise in 1996 net profits, was up HK$0.40 at HK$7.35.
China Resources Enterprise Ltd rose HK$0.40 at HK$21.60 and Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd was up HK$0.70 at HK$41.70.
HSBC Holdings Plc dropped HK$1.00 to HK$188.50 and Hang Seng Bank Ltd was down HK$0.50 at HK$85.00.
Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd fell HK$0.75 to HK$67.75 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd was off HK$1.00 at HK$65.00
